A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynamicScaler, with readable and matchable text, equations, figures, and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains appendix pages; v1 references an appendix that is unavailable within the supplied material.

before.justification: V1 reports original generated videos, evaluation using 100 video cases, a 20-participant user study, and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 retains the original quantitative evaluation, user study, and ablation results, and adds qualitative ablation outputs in Figure 8.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated image-to-video backbone from DynamiCrafter to VideoCrafter1, a limited reported model-component revision. The OSD, GMG, panoramic projection, and temporal shifting framework remains intact; the rewritten descriptions do not establish a broader algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions cover regular and 360-degree panoramic video generation, text and image conditioning, and long or loopable videos. The revised examples and added ablation visuals remain within this coverage; no distinct dataset or task is introduced.

E2.justification: The quantitative comparator remains 360DVD. The user study retains 360DVD for same-case comparisons and 360DVD, 4K4DGen, ScaleCrafter, and VividDream for random-case comparisons. VideoCrafter1 is identified as a backbone, not an added comparator.

E3.justification: The stated I2V experimental model changes from DynamiCrafter to VideoCrafter1 in Section 4.1. The 100-case evaluation, random camera views, evaluation metrics, and 20-participant study remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun following the model-description revision.

E4.justification: V2 Figure 8 adds visual comparisons of the full method, removal of GMG, and removal of OSD for balloon and blossom scenes, supplementing the unchanged numerical ablations. Figure 7 also expands the illustrated boundary-continuity cases.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All 66 metric scores and user ratings in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. Qualitative evidence changes through the added ablation outputs in Figure 8, revised continuity examples in Figure 7, and removal of v1 Figure 4's broader generation gallery.

T1.justification: V1 Equation 3's spherical-to-image mapping using arccos(y) and arcsin(z) is replaced by longitude atan2(y,x), latitude arcsin(z), and an explicit inverse mapping in v2 Equations 3–4. This corrects a localized mathematical definition; the remaining reformulations largely express existing procedures rather than introduce new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free, spatially scalable panoramic video generation with coherent motion, seamless boundaries, and long or loopable outputs. Revised component names and section titles do not materially change those claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 add substantive explanations of overlap across denoising steps and why early layout formation motivates GMG. Section 4.3 qualifies the user-study claim to highest ratings in most criteria, consistent with the retained graphics-quality ratings of 4.5 for 4K4DGen versus 4.3 for DynamicScaler.

D1.justification: V2 revises the named I2V implementation backbone and explicitly documents temporal clip splitting, concatenation, and boundary padding in Section 3.4. The project-page pointer also changes to a /new address; its contents or availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to VideoCrafter1 and Localizing Object-Level Shape Variations with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models, while removing DynamiCrafter. It also explicitly contrasts OSD with SpotDiffusion's random window shifting and expands the discussion of 4K4DGen's projection approach, without substantially changing the overall positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 substantially rewrite the technical narrative, replacing broad descriptions with explicit window operations, projection explanations, and temporal processing details. Related work gains numbered subsections, the projection discussion is subdivided, and terminology is made more consistent in the conclusion.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reorganized beside the abstract, Figure 3 is redrawn to show overlap across steps, and new temporal and ablation figures are added. V1's full-page generation gallery is removed, tables move into the experiment section, and Table 1 replaces video-length entries with an unlimited-length indicator.

improvement.justification: V2 improves technical clarity through the corrected projection mapping, clearer OSD/GMG and temporal explanations, and targeted visual ablations. It also better qualifies the user-study interpretation. These gains are limited: quantitative validation remains unchanged, the backbone revision is unexplained, and removing v1 Figure 4 reduces illustrative breadth.
